records.source: מִֽי־יִתְּנֵ֣נִי בַמִּדְבָּ֗ר מְלוֹן֙ אֹֽרְחִ֔ים וְאֶֽעֶזְבָה֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וְאֵלְכָ֖ה מֵֽאִתָּ֑ם כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים עֲצֶ֖רֶת בֹּגְדִֽים׃
records.gloss: Who will give me in the wilderness a lodging place of travelers, and I will leave my people and go from them; for all of them [are] adulterers, an assembly of treacherous [ones].
pieces: If only I had a travelers' shelter in the wilderness, \q so that I could leave my people and go far away from them! \q For they are all adulterers, \q a crowd of traitors.

L.1: Who will give me in the wilderness a lodging place of travelers, \q that I may leave my people and go away from them! \q For all of them [are] adulterers, \q an assembly of treacherous [ones].

R.1: I wish I had a place in the desert where travelers stop for the night. \q Then I could leave my people and get away from them. \q For they all commit adultery. \q They are a crowd of people who break faith.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: Hebrew 9:1-25 is 9:2-26 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 8 ends with verse 23 ("Oh that my head were waters ..."), which many Bibles number 9:1, and so this verse and the rest of the chapter (9:1-25 here) are numbered 9:2-26 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ. Jeremiah is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: who will give me: a wish; the speaker is most likely the prophet, still grieving as in 8:23
decisions.reason: "Who will give me ...?" is the usual Hebrew way of saying "If only I had ...", the same words that open 8:23. There the prophet wishes he could weep day and night for his people; here he wishes he could get away from them. The poem gives no name, and from verse 2 on the LORD speaks ("they do not know me, declares the LORD"), so the wish may also be heard as God's own, weary of a people who betray him. Prophet and God grieve with one voice in these chapters.

decisions.choice: a lodging place of travelers: a bare overnight shelter on a desert route
decisions.reason: This was the simplest kind of stopping place on a road through empty country: a spot with shelter, perhaps water, where people on the move spent a night. Even that lonely place would be better than living among his own people.

decisions.choice: adulterers ... an assembly of treacherous: faithless to their marriages and to their God
decisions.reason: Jeremiah charges the people with real adultery (5:7-8; 7:9) and also uses marriage unfaithfulness as a picture of turning from God (3:8-9). The word for "assembly" usually means a solemn gathering for worship (Isaiah 1:13; Joel 1:14); here it is a gathering of people who break faith, which sharpens the charge.

decisions.choice: If only I had ... / I wish I had; a crowd of traitors / people who break faith
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the Hebrew idiom of wishing ("who will give me") as a plain English wish. Readable says "commit adultery" and spells out "treacherous" as people who break faith.

records.source: וַֽיַּדְרְכ֤וּ אֶת־לְשׁוֹנָם֙ קַשְׁתָּ֣ם שֶׁ֔קֶר וְלֹ֥א לֶאֱמוּנָ֖ה גָּבְר֣וּ בָאָ֑רֶץ כִּי֩ מֵרָעָ֨ה אֶל־רָעָ֧ה׀יָצָ֛אוּ וְאֹתִ֥י לֹֽא־יָדָ֖עוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And they bend their tongue, their bow, [of] falsehood, and not for faithfulness they are strong in the land; for from evil to evil they go out, and me they do not know, declares Yahweh.
pieces: They bend their tongues like bows to shoot lies; \q they have grown strong in the land, but not by truth. \q For they go on from one evil to the next, and they do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: And they bend their tongue, their bow, [for] falsehood, \q and not for faithfulness are they strong in the land; \q for from evil to evil they go out, and {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they do not know, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: Their tongues are like bows, ready to shoot lies. \q They have become powerful in the land, but not by being honest. \q They go from one evil thing to another. They do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: they bend their tongue, their bow: the tongue is a bow drawn to shoot lies
decisions.reason: To "bend" a bow is to bend it to string it, ready to shoot. The Hebrew sets "their tongue" and "their bow" side by side: their tongue is their weapon, and its arrows are lies (verse 7; Psalm 64:4).

decisions.choice: not for faithfulness are they strong: their power in the land does not rest on truth
decisions.reason: The word means faithfulness, reliability, truth kept (5:1, 3; 7:28). They have become strong in the land, but not by faithfulness and not to serve it; their strength rests on lying.

decisions.choice: they do not know me: they do not acknowledge the LORD or live in his covenant
decisions.reason: To "know" the LORD is more than knowing about him: it is to acknowledge him and live faithfully toward him (Hosea 4:1, 6; Jeremiah 22:16). The charge returns in verse 5 and is answered in verse 23, where knowing the LORD is the one thing worth boasting of.

decisions.choice: like bows to shoot lies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "like" and "to shoot" to make the picture of the tongue as a bow clear (meaning decision m1).

records.source: אִ֤ישׁ מֵרֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ הִשָּׁמֵ֔רוּ וְעַל־כָּל־אָ֖ח אַל־תִּבְטָ֑חוּ כִּ֤י כָל־אָח֙ עָק֣וֹב יַעְקֹ֔ב וְכָל־רֵ֖עַ רָכִ֥יל יַהֲלֹֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Each from his neighbor guard yourselves, and on any brother do not trust; for every brother supplanting supplants, and every neighbor [as a] slanderer goes about.
pieces: Be on guard, every one of you, against your neighbor, \q and put no trust in any brother. \q For every brother is a cheat like Jacob, \q and every neighbor goes around spreading slander.

L.3: Each [of you], be on guard against your neighbor, \q and do not trust in any brother; \q for every brother surely supplants, \q and every neighbor goes about [as] a slanderer.

R.3: Each of you, watch out for your neighbors. \q Do not trust even your own brother. \q For every brother cheats, as Jacob cheated his brother. \q Every neighbor goes around telling lies about others.

decisions.choice: every brother surely supplants: a play on the name Jacob, who cheated his brother
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says, word for word, "every brother supplanting supplants" (*'aqov ya'qov*), and the second word is written with the same letters as the name Jacob (*ya'aqov*). The verb means to grab by the heel, to trip up from behind, to cheat someone out of what is theirs. Jacob was born holding his brother's heel (Genesis 25:26), and Esau said of him, "Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times" (Genesis 27:36; compare Hosea 12:4). Jeremiah says the people of Jacob have all become like their ancestor at his worst: every brother cheats his brother.

decisions.choice: every neighbor goes about as a slanderer: the words of the law in Leviticus 19:16
decisions.reason: The phrase "go about as a slanderer" is the one used in the law, "You shall not go about as a slanderer among your people" (Leviticus 19:16). The word means someone who carries tales from house to house, spreading gossip and false charges (6:28).

decisions.choice: neighbor ... brother: those closest to you, relatives and fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: "Neighbor" is the person next to you, a friend or fellow citizen; "brother" is a relative or fellow Israelite. When even these cannot be trusted, the whole society has broken down (12:6; Micah 7:5-6).

decisions.choice: a cheat like Jacob / cheats, as Jacob cheated his brother
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jacob, so that the reader hears the wordplay that the Hebrew carries in the verb itself (meaning decision m1). The name is not written in the Hebrew.

records.heading: Do not trust any neighbor

records.source: וְאִ֤ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ יְהָתֵ֔לּוּ וֶאֱמֶ֖ת לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ לִמְּד֧וּ לְשׁוֹנָ֛ם דַּבֶּר־שֶׁ֖קֶר הַעֲוֵ֥ה נִלְאֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And each [one] his neighbor they deceive, and truth they do not speak; they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood; to do iniquity they weary themselves.
pieces: Everyone cheats {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, \q and no one speaks the truth. \q They have trained their tongues to tell lies; they wear themselves out doing wrong.

L.4: And each one deceives {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, \q and they do not speak truth; \q they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood; they weary themselves doing iniquity.

R.4: They all cheat one another. \q No one tells the truth. \q They have taught themselves to lie, and they work so hard at doing wrong that they wear themselves out.

decisions.choice: deceives: cheats, makes a fool of
decisions.reason: The verb means to trifle with someone, to mock or cheat them. Jacob used it of Laban: "your father has cheated me" (Genesis 31:7), so the picture of verse 3 goes on.

decisions.choice: they weary themselves doing iniquity: they exhaust themselves in wrongdoing
decisions.reason: Doing wrong has become hard work that they pursue until they are worn out. They put more effort into sin than it would take to do right.

decisions.choice: taught themselves to lie; work so hard ... that they wear themselves out
decisions.reason: Readable says "taught themselves" for "taught their tongue" and spells out what it means to weary oneself in wrongdoing.

records.source: שִׁבְתְּךָ֖ בְּת֣וֹךְ מִרְמָ֑ה בְּמִרְמָ֛ה מֵאֲנ֥וּ דַֽעַת־אוֹתִ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Your dwelling [is] in [the] midst of deceit; in deceit they refuse to know me, declares Yahweh.
pieces: You live surrounded by deceit; \q in their deceit they refuse to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.5: Your dwelling [is] in the midst of deceit; \q in deceit they refuse to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.5: You live among people who lie and cheat. \q They are so full of lies that they refuse to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: your dwelling: the LORD speaks to the prophet
decisions.reason: "Your" is singular. The LORD turns to Jeremiah, who had wished to get away from his people (verse 1): he lives in the middle of a deceitful people.

decisions.choice: in the midst of deceit; in deceit: the Hebrew text as written
alternatives: oppression upon oppression, deceit upon deceit
decisions.reason: The consonants of this line can also be divided into different words, giving "oppression upon oppression, deceit upon deceit; they refuse to know me". The Greek translation reads something like that. The Hebrew as it stands makes good sense: Jeremiah lives among deceit, and deceit is why they refuse to know the LORD.

decisions.choice: They are so full of lies that they refuse
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link between deceit and their refusal explicit, which the Hebrew "in deceit" implies.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י צוֹרְפָ֖ם וּבְחַנְתִּ֑ים כִּֽי־אֵ֣יךְ אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts: here I [am] refining them, and I will test them; for how shall I act because of [the] daughter of my people?
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q I am going to refine them and put them to the test, \q for how else can I deal with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear people?

L.6: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q See, I am refining them, and I will test them; \q for how [else] shall I act because of the daughter of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people?

R.6: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q I am going to put them through fire to make them pure, and I will test them. \q What else can I do, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have sinned like this?

decisions.choice: refining and testing: heating metal to separate the pure from the waste
decisions.reason: A metalworker melted silver or gold in a furnace so that the waste (dross) separated from it, and tested the result. God will put his people through suffering to purge them. Jeremiah had already been told that the refining of this people was in vain, because the wicked are not removed (6:27-30).

decisions.choice: how shall I act because of the daughter of my people: a question that means there is nothing else to do
decisions.reason: The question expects no answer: given what his people have become, the LORD has no other course. The Greek translation reads "because of the evil of the daughter of my people", saying outright what the Hebrew leaves implied.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: a tender name for the people
decisions.reason: As at its first use in Jeremiah, "daughter of my people" speaks of the people as a beloved daughter; it carries love and grief, not contempt (8:21-23).

decisions.choice: put them through fire to make them pure; when my people have sinned like this
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of refining and says what "because of" points to: the people's sin (meaning decision m2).

records.source: חֵ֥ץ שָׁח֛וּט לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם מִרְמָ֣ה דִבֵּ֑ר בְּפִ֗יו שָׁל֤וֹם אֶת־רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ יְדַבֵּ֔רוּבְקִרְבּ֖וֹ יָשִׂ֥ים אָרְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: An arrow sharpened [is] their tongue; deceit it speaks; with his mouth peace with his neighbor he speaks, and in his inside he sets his ambush.
pieces: Their tongue is a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit. \q With their mouths they speak peace to their neighbors, \q but in their hearts they set an ambush for them.

L.7: Their tongue [is] a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit; \q with {{gender:their|his}} mouth one speaks peace to {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, \q but inwardly {{gender:they set their|he sets his}} ambush.

R.7: Their tongues are like sharp arrows. They tell lies. \q They speak words of peace to their neighbors, \q but inside they are planning to trap them.

decisions.choice: a sharpened arrow: the reading of the Hebrew margin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text as written has "a slaughtering arrow", a deadly arrow; the reading given in the margin, which this translation follows, has a word meaning "hammered" or "sharpened", used of beaten gold in 1 Kings 10:16-17. Either way the tongue is a weapon that kills.

decisions.choice: speaks peace: gives friendly greetings
decisions.reason: To "speak peace" with someone is to greet them warmly and wish them well (Psalm 28:3). The friendly words hide a plan to harm.

decisions.choice: in his inside he sets his ambush: inwardly he lies in wait
decisions.reason: An ambush is a hidden trap for an enemy (Joshua 8:2). The deceiver's heart is the hiding place where he waits for the moment to strike the neighbor he greets.

decisions.choice: plural: they speak ... their neighbors
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves from "their tongue" to a single representative person ("his mouth", "his neighbor"). Balanced and Readable keep the plural throughout, which says the same thing about everyone.

records.source: הַעַל־אֵ֥לֶּה לֹֽא־אֶפְקָד־בָּ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה אִ֚ם בְּג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר־כָּזֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃ס
records.gloss: For these [things] shall I not punish them, declares Yahweh? Or on a nation which [is] like this shall not my soul avenge itself?
pieces: Should I not punish them for these things? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q On a nation such as this \q should I not take vengeance?

L.8: Shall I not punish them for these things? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Or on a nation such as this \q shall not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul avenge itself?

R.8: Should I not punish them for doing these things? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Should I not pay back a nation like this?

decisions.choice: the same refrain as 5:9 and 5:29
decisions.reason: These words repeat almost exactly the question of 5:9 and 5:29. Each time it ends a list of the people's wrongs: can the LORD let such things go?

decisions.choice: punish ... avenge itself: the rightful judge gives what is due
decisions.reason: The verb for "punish" means to visit, to come and deal with someone. To "avenge" here is not spite but the just answer of the rightful judge to wrongs done (Deuteronomy 32:35). "My soul" means "I myself".

decisions.choice: take vengeance / pay back, as in 5:9
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded as in 5:9 and 5:29 at every level (m1). Balanced and Readable say "take vengeance" and "pay back" for "my soul avenge itself", which is not natural English.

records.source: עַל־הֶ֨הָרִ֜ים אֶשָּׂ֧א בְכִ֣י וָנֶ֗הִי וְעַל־נְא֤וֹת מִדְבָּר֙ קִינָ֔ה כִּ֤י נִצְּתוּ֙ מִבְּלִי־אִ֣ישׁ עֹבֵ֔ר וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ ק֣וֹל מִקְנֶ֑ה מֵע֤וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֔ה נָדְד֖וּ הָלָֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: For the mountains I will take up weeping and wailing, and for [the] pastures of [the] wilderness a lament, for they are burned without anyone passing through, and they do not hear [the] sound of livestock; from [the] bird of the heavens and to [the] beast they have fled, they have gone.
pieces: I will weep and wail for the mountains, and raise a lament for the pastures in the wilderness, \q because they are scorched and no one travels through them, \q and no one hears the lowing of cattle. \q The birds of the sky and the animals \q have all fled and are gone.

L.9: For the mountains I will take up weeping and wailing, and for the pastures of the wilderness a lament, \q for they are burned, with no one passing through, \q and they do not hear the sound of livestock; \q from the birds of the heavens to the beasts, \q they have fled, they are gone.

R.9: I will cry and mourn for the mountains. \q I will sing a sad song for the grasslands in the wild country. \q They are burned up, and no one travels through them. \q No one hears cattle mooing there. \q The birds and the animals have all run away.

decisions.choice: I will take up: the speaker weeps for the land
alternatives: Take up weeping (a command to the people)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "I will take up", and does not say whether the prophet or the LORD is weeping; the LORD speaks in verse 10. The Greek translation reads a plural command, "Take up weeping".

decisions.choice: burned: scorched, laid waste
decisions.reason: The verb means to be burned or set on fire. A similar verb in verse 11 means "laid waste", and the two pictures meet: the land is a burned-out waste where no one passes.

decisions.choice: pastures of the wilderness: open grazing land
decisions.reason: The "wilderness" here is not sand desert but open country beyond the farms, where flocks and herds grazed (23:10; Psalm 65:13). Even the animals and birds have left it.

decisions.choice: sing a sad song; grasslands in the wild country; cattle mooing
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "lament", "pastures of the wilderness" and "the sound of livestock".

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לְגַלִּ֖ים מְע֣וֹן תַּנִּ֑ים וְאֶת־עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה אֶתֵּ֥ן שְׁמָמָ֖ה מִבְּלִ֖י יוֹשֵֽׁב׃ס
records.gloss: And I will make Jerusalem into heaps, a lair of jackals, and [the] cities of Judah I will make a desolation without inhabitant.
pieces: I will turn Jerusalem into a heap of ruins, a den for jackals, \q and I will make the towns of Judah a wasteland where no one lives.

L.10: And I will make Jerusalem into heaps, a den of jackals, \q and the cities of Judah I will make a desolation without inhabitant.

R.10: I will turn Jerusalem into piles of stones where jackals live. \q I will make the towns of Judah empty ruins where no one lives.

decisions.choice: I will make: the LORD now speaks
decisions.reason: The "I" of this verse is the LORD, who brings the ruin that verse 9 mourns.

decisions.choice: heaps, a den of jackals: a city turned to rubble where wild animals live
decisions.reason: "Heaps" are piles of stones from fallen buildings. Jackals, wild dogs that live in packs, make their dens in ruins far from people; to call a city their home is to say no one lives there any more (10:22; 49:33; Isaiah 34:13).

decisions.choice: towns of Judah
decisions.reason: The word covers walled places of every size; Balanced and Readable say "towns" for the many smaller places of Judah, as English usually does.

records.source: מִֽי־הָאִ֤ישׁ הֶֽחָכָם֙ וְיָבֵ֣ן אֶת־זֹ֔את וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר פִּֽי־יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו וְיַגִּדָ֑הּ עַל־מָה֙ אָבְדָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ נִצְּתָ֥ה כַמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִבְּלִ֖י עֹבֵֽר׃ס
records.gloss: Who [is] the man, the wise, and he will understand this, and [the one] whom [the] mouth of Yahweh has spoken to him, and he may declare it? For what has perished the land, [is it] laid waste like the wilderness without [one] passing through?
pieces: Who is wise enough to understand this? \q To whom has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken, so that {{gender:they|he}} can explain it? \q Why has the land been ruined \q and laid waste like a wilderness that no one crosses?

L.11: Who [is] {{gender:the wise one|the wise man}}, that {{gender:they|he}} may understand this? \q And to whom has the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken, that {{gender:they|he}} may declare it? \q Why has the land perished, \q laid waste like the wilderness, with no one passing through?

R.11: Who is wise enough to understand this? \q Who has heard from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and can explain it? \q Why has the land been ruined? \q Why has it become an empty waste like a desert, where no one travels?

decisions.choice: who ... why: questions that only the LORD can answer
decisions.reason: No wise person steps forward. The questions show that human wisdom cannot explain the ruin; the answer comes in verse 12 from the LORD himself. The wise man here prepares for verse 22, where the wise are told not to boast in their wisdom.

decisions.choice: the mouth of the LORD has spoken: the LORD himself has spoken
decisions.reason: "The mouth of the LORD" stresses that the words come directly from God (Isaiah 1:20; 40:5). Only someone the LORD has spoken to can declare why the land lies in ruins.

decisions.choice: Who is wise enough to understand this?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "Who is the wise man, that he may understand this?" as a single natural question with the same meaning.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־עָזְבָם֙ אֶת־תּ֣וֹרָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְלֹא־שָׁמְע֥וּ בְקוֹלִ֖י וְלֹא־הָ֥לְכוּ בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh: because they have forsaken my instruction which I set before them, and not they have listened to my voice and not walked in it,
pieces: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered: \q It is because they have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction, which I set before them; \q they have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice or followed it,

L.12: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said: \q Because they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction, which I set before them, \q and have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, and have not walked in it,

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered: \q It is because they have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching, which I gave them. \q They have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or lived by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching.

decisions.choice: my instruction: the LORD's teaching for his people's life
decisions.reason: The word (*torah*) means instruction or teaching. It includes the laws given through Moses, but its sense is wider: all the LORD has taught his people about how to live with him (2:8; 8:8).

decisions.choice: listened to my voice ... walked in it: obeyed and lived by it
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone is to obey them; to "walk in" an instruction is to live by it day by day (7:23; 26:4).

decisions.choice: the LORD said: the answer to the questions of verse 11
decisions.reason: The LORD answers the question no wise person could. His answer runs through verses 12-13 and leads to the sentence in verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: answered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "answered" for "said", because the LORD is replying to the questions of verse 11 (meaning decision m3). Readable also says "obeyed me" for "listened to my voice" and repeats "my teaching" to make clear what "it" refers to.

records.source: וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י שְׁרִר֣וּת לִבָּ֑ם וְאַחֲרֵי֙ הַבְּעָלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִמְּד֖וּם אֲבוֹתָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And they have walked after [the] stubbornness of their heart and after the Baals, which their fathers taught them.
pieces: but have followed the stubbornness of their own hearts \q and gone after the Baals, as their ancestors taught them.

L.13: and they have walked after the stubbornness of their heart \q and after the Baals, as their fathers taught them.

R.13: Instead, they have stubbornly followed their own hearts. \q They have followed the Baals, false gods called Baal, just as their ancestors taught them.

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of their heart: doing what they themselves want, against God
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Deuteronomy 29:18, of the person who says "I will be safe though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart", and Jeremiah uses it often (3:17; 7:24; 11:8). The heart is the seat of the will; they follow their own will instead of the LORD's voice. Here the word "evil", which the phrase has in some places, is not used.

decisions.choice: the Baals: the many local forms of the god Baal
decisions.reason: Baal was the Canaanite storm god, worshiped as the giver of rain and crops. He was honored at many local shrines under different titles, so the Bible often speaks of "the Baals" in the plural (2:23; Judges 2:11).

decisions.choice: as their fathers taught them: idolatry handed down from earlier generations
decisions.reason: The relative word can mean "which" (the Baals, which their fathers taught them about) or "as". Either way the worship of Baal was something learned from parents and grandparents (7:18; 16:11-12).

decisions.choice: followed; ancestors; the Baals, false gods called Baal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "followed" for "walked after" and "ancestors" for "fathers", which here means earlier generations. Readable explains who the Baals were, as this book does elsewhere.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֧י מַאֲכִילָ֛ם אֶת־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה לַֽעֲנָ֑ה וְהִשְׁקִיתִ֖ים מֵי־רֹֽאשׁ׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: here I [am] feeding them, this people, wormwood, and I will give them to drink water of poison.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: \q I am going to feed this people bitter wormwood \q and give them poisoned water to drink.

L.14: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: \q See, I am feeding them, this people, wormwood, \q and I will give them poisoned water to drink.

R.14: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: \q I am going to give these people bitter plants to eat \q and poisoned water to drink.

decisions.choice: wormwood ... poison: a bitter plant and a poisonous one
decisions.reason: Wormwood is a plant with a very bitter taste (Amos 5:7; Lamentations 3:15, 19). The word joined to "water" names a poisonous plant, perhaps the poppy or hemlock; the exact plant is not known. Together they picture suffering that is bitter and deadly.

decisions.choice: wormwood and poison: the warning of Deuteronomy 29:17
decisions.reason: Moses warned that anyone who turned from the LORD to other gods would be "a root bearing poison and wormwood" (Deuteronomy 29:17), in the passage that also speaks of the stubbornness of the heart (29:18; verse 13 here). The bitter fruit of their idolatry is now given back to them. The same words return in 23:15, and the poisoned water in 8:14.

decisions.choice: feeding them ... giving them to drink: the LORD himself sends the suffering
decisions.reason: Food and drink stand for what a person receives in life. The LORD who once fed his people in the wilderness now gives them bitterness to eat and drink.

decisions.choice: bitter wormwood / bitter plants
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "bitter" to tell the reader what wormwood is like; Readable says "bitter plants" for the unfamiliar name.

records.source: וַהֲפִֽצוֹתִים֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ הֵ֖מָּה וַֽאֲבוֹתָ֑ם וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־הַחֶ֔רֶב עַ֥ד כַּלּוֹתִ֖י אוֹתָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And I will scatter them among the nations which not they have known, they and their fathers, and I will send after them the sword until I have consumed them.
pieces: I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known, \q and I will send the sword to pursue them until I have finished them off.

L.15: And I will scatter them among the nations that they have not known, they and their fathers, \q and I will send the sword after them until I have made an end of them.

R.15: I will scatter them among nations that they and their ancestors never knew. \q I will send war after them until I have destroyed them.

decisions.choice: scatter ... among the nations ... send the sword after them: the curses of the covenant
decisions.reason: The words echo the warnings of the law: "I will scatter you among the nations and draw out the sword after you" (Leviticus 26:33), and "the LORD will scatter you among all the peoples ... gods which neither you nor your fathers have known" (Deuteronomy 28:64; compare 28:36).

decisions.choice: until I have made an end of them: the threat in its full force
decisions.reason: The verb means to finish, to bring to an end. Elsewhere the LORD says he will not make a full end of his people (4:27; 5:10, 18; 30:11). Here the sentence is stated in its full strength, as the covenant curses state it; the hope of a remnant is not in view in this verse.

decisions.choice: war; destroyed them
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for "the sword", as this book does in the list "sword, famine and disease", and "destroyed them" for "made an end of them".

records.source: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ וְקִרְא֥וּ לַמְקוֹנְנ֖וֹת וּתְבוֹאֶ֑ינָה וְאֶל־הַחֲכָמ֥וֹת שִׁלְח֖וּ וְתָבֽוֹאנָה׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: consider and call for the mourning women, and let them come; and to the skillful [women] send, and let them come,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q Think about what is happening, and call for the mourning women; let them come. \q Send for the women who are skilled in lament; let them come,

L.16: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q Consider, and call for the mourning women, that they may come; \q and send for the skillful women, that they may come,

R.16: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q Think about this! Call for the women whose work is to mourn the dead. Tell them to come. \q Send for the women who know how to sing songs of grief. Tell them to come.

decisions.choice: the mourning women ... the skillful women: women who led the laments at funerals
decisions.reason: In Israel, as among its neighbors, mourning for the dead was led by women who knew the traditional laments and could stir others to weep (Amos 5:16; 2 Chronicles 35:25). "Skillful" is the word for "wise" used of a craft (Exodus 35:25); these women were skilled at their task and were called in when someone died. Now they are summoned to mourn a whole nation.

decisions.choice: consider, and call: the people are addressed
decisions.reason: The commands are plural and spoken to the people. They are to take in what is coming and prepare for a funeral, their own.

decisions.choice: Think about what is happening; whose work is to mourn the dead
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "consider" has no object; Balanced and Readable supply one. Readable explains who the mourning women were (meaning decision m1).

records.heading: Call for the mourning women

records.source: וּתְמַהֵ֕רְנָה וְתִשֶּׂ֥נָה עָלֵ֖ינוּ נֶ֑הִי וְתֵרַ֤דְנָה עֵינֵ֨ינוּ֙ דִּמְעָ֔ה וְעַפְעַפֵּ֖ינוּ יִזְּלוּ־מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And let them hurry and raise over us wailing, and let our eyes run down [with] tears, and our eyelids flow [with] water.
pieces: and let them hurry and raise a wailing over us, \q so that our eyes overflow with tears \q and water streams from our eyelids.

L.17: and let them hurry and raise a wailing over us, \q that our eyes may run down with tears \q and our eyelids flow with water.

R.17: Let them hurry and cry out in grief for us. \q Then our eyes will fill with tears, \q and water will pour from our eyelids.

decisions.choice: over us: the voice of the people
decisions.reason: The speaker now says "us": the people themselves, or the prophet speaking as one of them. The professional mourners are to start the lament so that everyone else can weep.

decisions.choice: eyes run down with tears: weeping without stopping
decisions.reason: The picture of eyes running with water is a way of saying grief has no end (8:23; 13:17; 14:17; Lamentations 1:16).

decisions.choice: cry out in grief
decisions.reason: Readable says "cry out in grief" for "raise a wailing".

records.source: כִּ֣י ק֥וֹל נְהִ֛י נִשְׁמַ֥ע מִצִּיּ֖וֹן אֵ֣יךְ שֻׁדָּ֑דְנוּ בֹּ֤שְׁנֽוּ מְאֹד֙ כִּֽי־עָזַ֣בְנוּ אָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י הִשְׁלִ֖יכוּ מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֵֽינוּ׃ס
records.gloss: For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion: How we are ruined! We are ashamed greatly, for we have left [the] land, for they have cast down our dwellings.
pieces: For the sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are ruined! \q How deep is our shame! We have had to leave the land, \q because our homes have been torn down."

L.18: For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are ruined! \q We are greatly ashamed, for we have left the land, \q for they have thrown down our dwellings."

R.18: Listen! People in Zion are crying loudly: "We are destroyed! \q We are so ashamed! We have had to leave our land. \q Our homes have been torn down."

decisions.choice: they have thrown down our dwellings: the enemy has torn the houses down
alternatives: our dwellings have cast us out
decisions.reason: The verb is plural and active with no named subject: "they", the enemy, have thrown down the people's homes. It can also be read with the dwellings as subject: "our dwellings have thrown us out".

decisions.choice: greatly ashamed: utterly disgraced by defeat
decisions.reason: To be put to shame is to have one's hopes collapse in public, as happens to a defeated people (2:36; 20:11). It is more than a feeling of embarrassment.

decisions.choice: we have left the land: exile
decisions.reason: To leave the land is to go into exile, losing the land the LORD gave to the ancestors. The lament mourns this as if it has already happened.

decisions.choice: had to leave; our homes have been torn down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "had to" because the leaving is forced, and put "they have thrown down" as "have been torn down", since the Hebrew names no subject (meaning decision m1). Readable begins "Listen!" to show that the voices are heard.

records.source: כִּֽי־שְׁמַ֤עְנָה נָשִׁים֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה וְתִקַּ֥ח אָזְנְכֶ֖ם דְּבַר־פִּ֑יו וְלַמֵּ֤דְנָה בְנֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ נֶ֔הִי וְאִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָ֖הּ קִינָֽה׃
records.gloss: For hear, women, [the] word of Yahweh, and let your ear receive [the] word of his mouth; and teach your daughters wailing, and [each] woman her neighbor a lament.
pieces: Now, you women, listen to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q let your ears take in the word from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth. \q Teach your daughters a song of mourning, \q and teach one another a lament.

L.19: Now hear, you women, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and let your ear receive the word of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth; \q teach your daughters a wailing, \q and each woman her neighbor a lament.

R.19: Women, listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. \q Pay attention to the words {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks. \q Teach your daughters to sing sad songs. \q Teach one another songs for the dead.

decisions.choice: teach your daughters ... each woman her neighbor: more mourners will be needed
decisions.reason: Laments were learned and handed on, mother to daughter and woman to woman. The dead will be so many (verses 20-21) that the skilled women alone will not be enough; every woman must learn to mourn.

decisions.choice: lament: a funeral song
decisions.reason: This word names a song sung over the dead, often with a short, limping beat (2 Samuel 1:17; the book of Lamentations). The word for "wailing" beside it is a cry of grief.

decisions.choice: now hear ... your ear: women are addressed
decisions.reason: The opening word stresses the call to listen. The commands are addressed to women, while "your ear" uses the form normally used for men; Hebrew often uses that form for a mixed or general group.

decisions.choice: one another
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "one another" for "each woman her neighbor".

records.source: כִּֽי־עָ֤לָה מָ֨וֶת֙ בְּחַלּוֹנֵ֔ינוּ בָּ֖א בְּאַרְמְנוֹתֵ֑ינוּ לְהַכְרִ֤ית עוֹלָל֙ מִח֔וּץ בַּחוּרִ֖ים מֵרְחֹבֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: For death has come up in our windows, it has entered in our fortresses, to cut off [the] child from [the] street, young men from [the] squares.
pieces: For death has climbed in through our windows \q and entered our strongholds, \q to cut off the children from the streets \q and the young men from the public squares.

L.20: For death has come up through our windows; \q it has entered our fortresses, \q to cut off the child from the street, \q young men from the squares.

R.20: Death has climbed in through our windows. \q It has come into our strong buildings. \q It takes the children from the streets \q and the young men from the town squares.

decisions.choice: death has come up through our windows: death as an intruder that no wall keeps out
decisions.reason: Death is pictured as a thief or raider climbing in where the doors are barred, getting even into the strongest houses. Stories told among Israel's neighbors spoke of Death as a power that devours the living, and the picture may draw on such ideas, but its sense here is plain: no one is safe anywhere.

decisions.choice: children from the street, young men from the squares: the places of daily life
decisions.reason: The streets were where children played and the squares were where young men gathered (Zechariah 8:4-5). Death empties the public places where the city's life and future were most visible.

decisions.choice: fortresses: strong houses, palaces
decisions.reason: The word means a large, fortified building, a palace or stronghold (Amos 3:10-11). Not even the homes of the powerful are safe.

decisions.choice: climbed in
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "climbed in" for "come up", which in this picture means climbing up to and through a window.

records.source: דַּבֵּ֗ר כֹּ֚ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְנָֽפְלָה֙ נִבְלַ֣ת הָֽאָדָ֔ם כְּדֹ֖מֶן עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּכְעָמִ֛יר מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י הַקֹּצֵ֖ר וְאֵ֥ין מְאַסֵּֽף׃ס
records.gloss: Speak: thus, declares Yahweh: and will fall [the] corpse of humankind like dung on [the] face of the field, and like cut grain from behind the reaper, and there is none gathering.
pieces: Say this, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Human corpses will fall like dung on the open field, \q like cut grain left behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.

L.21: Speak thus, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q The corpses of humankind will fall like dung on the open field, \q and like cut grain behind the reaper, with no one gathering [them].

R.21: Tell them this message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Dead bodies will lie on the open fields like manure. \q They will be like grain that harvesters cut and leave behind, and no one will gather them up.

decisions.choice: speak thus, declares the LORD: a command to the prophet inside the poem
decisions.reason: The LORD breaks in with an order to the prophet to announce what follows. The lament of verses 19-20 is followed by the LORD's own word on the dead.

decisions.choice: like cut grain behind the reaper, with no one gathering: the dead are left unburied
decisions.reason: At harvest the reaper cut the grain with a sickle and left the stalks lying in rows, and others followed to gather them into sheaves. Here the dead lie like those rows, but no one comes to gather them: there is no one left to bury them (8:2; 16:4; 25:33).

decisions.choice: like dung: a picture of utter disgrace
decisions.reason: To lie unburied like dung on a field was the worst shame a person could suffer (8:2; 16:4; 2 Kings 9:37).

decisions.choice: Tell them this message; manure; harvesters
decisions.reason: Readable puts the command as "Tell them this message" and uses plain words for "dung" and "reaper".

records.source: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־יִתְהַלֵּ֤ל חָכָם֙ בְּחָכְמָת֔וֹ וְאַל־יִתְהַלֵּ֥ל הַגִּבּ֖וֹר בִּגְבֽוּרָת֑וֹ אַל־יִתְהַלֵּ֥ל עָשִׁ֖יר בְּעָשְׁרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: let not boast [the] wise in his wisdom, and let not boast the mighty in his might; let not boast [the] rich in his riches.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: The wise must not boast about {{gender:their|his}} wisdom, the strong must not boast about {{gender:their|his}} strength, and the rich must not boast about {{gender:their|his}} wealth.

L.22: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Let not the wise boast in {{gender:their|his}} wisdom, and let not the mighty boast in {{gender:their|his}} might; let not the rich boast in {{gender:their|his}} riches.

R.22: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Wise people should not brag about how wise they are. Strong people should not brag about how strong they are. Rich people should not brag about how rich they are.

decisions.choice: boast: take pride in, rely on as one's glory
decisions.reason: The verb means to praise oneself, to make something one's pride and confidence. What a person boasts in is what they trust to make them secure and important.

decisions.choice: the wise, the mighty, the rich: the things a people trusted
decisions.reason: Wisdom, military strength and wealth were the marks of a successful nation and its leaders. Jeremiah has already shown the wise with no word from the LORD (8:8-9; verse 11 here), and the strong and rich will not be saved by what they have (5:27-28).

decisions.choice: a new saying in prose
decisions.reason: From here to the end of the chapter the text is prose, not poetry. The saying of verses 22-23 answers the question of verse 11: true wisdom is to know the LORD.

decisions.choice: the strong ... strength; wealth / brag
decisions.reason: Balanced says "strong" and "strength" for the warrior's might and "wealth" for riches. Readable says "brag about how wise they are", which says the same thing in plain words.

records.heading: Let the one who boasts boast in this

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־בְּזֹ֞את יִתְהַלֵּ֣ל הַמִּתְהַלֵּ֗ל הַשְׂכֵּל֮ וְיָדֹ֣עַ אוֹתִי֒ כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עֹ֥שֶׂה חֶ֛סֶד מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בָּאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־בְאֵ֥לֶּה חָפַ֖צְתִּי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: But rather in this let boast the [one] boasting: having insight and knowing me, that I [am] Yahweh doing loyal love, justice and righteousness in the earth; for in these I delight, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Instead, whoever boasts should boast of this: that they understand and know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who acts with loyal love, justice and righteousness on the earth. For these are what I delight in, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.23: But let the one who boasts boast in this: understanding and knowing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who does loyal love, justice and righteousness in the earth; for in these I delight, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.23: Instead, anyone who wants to brag should brag about this: that they understand {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I act with faithful love, justice and righteousness on the earth. These are the things that please {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: let the one who boasts boast in this: quoted by Paul
decisions.reason: Paul sums up this verse as "The one who boasts must boast in the Lord" (1 Corinthians 1:31; 2 Corinthians 10:17), setting God's wisdom in Christ against human wisdom, strength and status, as Jeremiah sets knowing the LORD against wisdom, might and riches.

decisions.choice: understanding and knowing me: knowing the LORD for who he is
decisions.reason: The two verbs say "having insight and knowing", without naming a person or a time. To "know" the LORD is to acknowledge him and live in his ways; Jeremiah later says that to do justice for the poor "is to know me" (22:16). It answers verses 2 and 5, where the people refuse to know him.

decisions.choice: loyal love, justice and righteousness: what the LORD does and loves
decisions.reason: Loyal love (*hesed*) is faithful, generous love kept within a covenant. Justice is setting things right, especially for the weak; righteousness is doing what is right by others. The LORD does these "in the earth", among people, and delights in them, so those who know him will do them too (22:3, 15-16).

decisions.choice: loyal love / faithful love
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable, as in Isaiah. Balanced and Readable put "understanding and knowing me" as "that they understand and know me", and Readable breaks the sentence into short sentences.

records.source: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וּפָ֣קַדְתִּ֔י עַל־כָּל־מ֖וּל בְּעָרְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: See, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, and I will punish every [one] circumcised in foreskin,
pieces: The time is coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will bring punishment on all who are circumcised yet uncircumcised,

L.24: See, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will punish all who are circumcised in the foreskin,

R.24: The time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will punish everyone who is circumcised only in body.

decisions.choice: circumcised in the foreskin: circumcised yet uncircumcised, the outward sign without the reality
decisions.reason: The phrase is a paradox: people who are circumcised and yet still "in foreskin". Verse 25 explains it: the nations are uncircumcised and Israel is uncircumcised in heart, so the outward mark does not protect anyone. The phrase can also be taken as "circumcised and uncircumcised alike", meaning everyone without exception; verse 25 favors the first reading.

decisions.choice: days are coming: a time the LORD will bring
decisions.reason: This formula announces a future act of God, whether of judgment (7:32; 19:6) or of restoration (16:14; 23:5; 31:31).

decisions.choice: punish: visit in judgment
decisions.reason: The verb means to visit, to come and deal with someone; with "on" it means to bring punishment (verse 8).

decisions.choice: circumcised only in body
decisions.reason: Readable puts the paradox in plain words: the people have the mark of circumcision on their bodies, but nothing more (meaning decision m1). Readable ends the sentence here and repeats "I will punish" in verse 25.

records.source: עַל־מִצְרַ֣יִם וְעַל־יְהוּדָ֗ה וְעַל־אֱד֞וֹם וְעַל־בְּנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ וְעַל־מוֹאָ֔ב וְעַל֙ כָּל־קְצוּצֵ֣י פֵאָ֔ה הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּ֤י כָל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ עֲרֵלִ֔ים וְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַרְלֵי־לֵֽב׃ס
records.gloss: on Egypt and on Judah and on Edom and on [the] sons of Ammon and on Moab and on all [those] clipped [at the] corner who dwell in the wilderness; for all the nations [are] uncircumcised, and all [the] house of Israel [are] uncircumcised of heart.
pieces: Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who clip the hair at their temples and live in the desert. For every one of these nations is uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.

L.25: on Egypt, and on Judah, and on Edom, and on the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon, and on Moab, and on all who are clipped [at the] corners, who live in the wilderness; for all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.

R.25: I will punish Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon and Moab. I will punish the desert tribes who cut their hair short at the sides. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the people of Israel are uncircumcised in heart: their hearts are closed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: Egypt, Edom, Ammon, Moab ... all the nations are uncircumcised: circumcision without covenant
decisions.reason: Circumcision was not only Israel's custom: the Egyptians practiced it, and some of Israel's neighbors seem to have done so too. To the LORD it means nothing in itself. Judah is listed among these nations, as one more people with the outward mark and no more.

decisions.choice: clipped at the corners: desert tribes who cut the hair at the sides of the head
alternatives: those who live in the far corners of the desert
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely describes the desert Arab tribes, who cut their hair short at the temples; Jeremiah uses it of them again in 25:23 and 49:32. Israel was told not to cut the hair at the sides of the head (Leviticus 19:27), perhaps because the custom was tied to other worship. The words could also mean "those who live in the far corners" of the desert; either way the same peoples are meant.

decisions.choice: uncircumcised in heart: a heart closed to the LORD
decisions.reason: The law speaks of an uncircumcised heart that must be humbled (Leviticus 26:41) and calls Israel to circumcise the foreskin of their hearts (Deuteronomy 10:16), a work the LORD himself promises to do (Deuteronomy 30:6). Jeremiah gave the same call (4:4). Israel, circumcised in body, is no better than the nations, because its heart is closed to God.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites; I will punish; their hearts are closed to me
decisions.reason: Balanced says "the Ammonites" for "the sons of Ammon". Readable repeats "I will punish" from verse 24 and explains "uncircumcised in heart" as Leviticus 26:41 does at Readable.
